subject: microbiology
title: Coxsackievirus, Hand Foot and Mouth Disease, Herpangina and Rhinovirus

steps.tx: **Coxsackieviruses** are enteroviruses divided historically into group A and B by pathology in newborn mice. Group A types are strongly linked with herpangina, hand foot and mouth disease and acute haemorrhagic conjunctivitis, whereas group B types are classic causes of pleurodynia, myocarditis and pericarditis. Modern PCR types enteroviruses molecularly, but the A and B pattern remains useful clinical shorthand.
steps.say: Coxsackie A favours mouth, hands and feet; Coxsackie B reaches pleura and heart.

left.title: Group A syndromes
points: Acute haemorrhagic conjunctivitis from A24 variant

steps.tx: **Hand foot and mouth disease** causes fever, painful oral ulcers and vesicular lesions on hands, feet and buttocks, most often from coxsackievirus A16 and enterovirus A71. EV A71 outbreaks can involve brainstem encephalitis, neurogenic pulmonary oedema and acute flaccid weakness. Hydration is the usual treatment priority because mouth pain reduces intake, while neurologic or cardiopulmonary signs demand hospital escalation.
steps.say: Most HFMD needs fluids and observation; EV A71 can become a brainstem emergency.

left.title: Typical mild disease
points: Nail shedding can occur weeks later

steps.tx: **Herpangina** is an acute febrile enanthem with vesicles and ulcers on the posterior palate, tonsillar pillars and soft palate. Unlike herpetic gingivostomatitis, lesions spare the anterior mouth and gums and are usually enteroviral. Pain and drooling may mimic bacterial pharyngitis, but posterior distribution and summer seasonality help. Antibiotics do not shorten uncomplicated herpangina.
steps.say: Posterior mouth ulcers in summer suggest herpangina, not anterior herpetic gingivostomatitis.

right.title: HSV gingivostomatitis
points: Anterior mouth and swollen bleeding gums

steps.tx: **Echoviruses** are enteroviruses named because they were originally enteric cytopathogenic human orphan viruses. They cause aseptic meningitis, rash, neonatal sepsis-like illness and chronic meningoencephalitis in people with agammaglobulinaemia. Like other enteroviruses they circulate in summer and autumn, spread faecal-orally and through respiratory secretions, and are diagnosed mainly by PCR from CSF, throat or stool.
steps.say: An orphan virus in name, echovirus is a familiar meningitis and neonatal pathogen in practice.

steps.tx: **Rhinoviruses** are picornaviruses adapted to the cooler nasal mucosa and are the dominant cause of common colds. They also trigger asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease exacerbations, and species C can cause severe wheeze in children. Their many types and limited cross-protection explain repeated colds and vaccine difficulty. PCR detects rhinovirus frequently, so a positive result must still fit the clinical syndrome.
steps.say: Rhinovirus is not merely a cold virus when it precipitates severe wheeze.

left.title: Biology
points: Species A, B and C with many types

right.title: Clinical weight
points: Bronchiolitis and pneumonia in vulnerable hosts

steps.tx: Enterovirus PCR from **cerebrospinal fluid** is more causally persuasive than stool PCR because enteroviruses can shed in stool for weeks. Blood PCR is useful in neonatal systemic disease. There is no routine specific antiviral for most enteroviruses; management is supportive, with immunoglobulin used in selected neonatal or antibody-deficiency infections. Pleconaril is not a standard widely available therapy.
steps.say: CSF enterovirus PCR proves meningitis better than a lingering positive stool.
